solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Versatile player daft men abandon

indicators.note: daft means silly or crazy, so the letters of the two words beside it are jumbled

parts.note: these two words supply the letters to be jumbled

explanation.surface: A band leader complains that foolish men walk out on the group.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-man band is a busker playing several instruments at once, hence a versatile performer.

clue.text: Part of concert that's not encored

definitions.note: an adjective phrase for an adverb: performed one time only

indicators.note: part of the word concert is taken, so the answer sits within it

parts.note: the answer runs inside this word, from its second letter

explanation.surface: A piece in a concert that got no repeat performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means a single time, so something done once was never repeated as an encore.

clue.text: One slip corrected using another?

definitions.meaning: a slip is a mistake, here one put right
another slip, this time a slip of paper inserted in a book

explanation.walkthrough: An erratum slip is a printed note slipped into a book to correct a misprint, so one slip fixes another.
explanation.definitionFit: An erratum is an error in print, and its correction is printed on a separate inserted sheet.

clue.text: Critical comment from part of UK in a crazy form

indicators.note: in puts the UK region inside the rest

parts.note: taken as written
mad means crazy
a version is one form of something
NI is Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A disparaging remark about a region expressed in some wild manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Animadversion is a formal word for censure, an adverse remark.

clue.text: Listed in programme as indisposed, so resting?

parts.note: someone who is resting is in bed
ill means indisposed, unwell

explanation.surface: An actor listed as appearing turns out to be ill and off sick.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a story: being ill, so in bed, which places the sick word inside the bed word.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer billed is named on the bill, the printed programme of a show.

clue.text: Extra handle in metal unfinished, holding worker up

indicators.note: holding means the cut metal contains the turned worker
unfinished drops the last letter

parts.note: nickel is a metallic element

indicators.note: up in a down clue means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a man is a worker on a team

explanation.surface: An additional grip fixed into a metal object, with someone above.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handle' is slang for a name, which is the sense the definition needs.
explanation.definitionFit: A nickname is an added informal name, and handle is slang for a name.

clue.text: Become engaged with some time-sharing

indicators.note: some of the phrase time-sharing is taken, so the answer lies inside its letters

parts.note: the answer spans the end of time and the start of sharing

explanation.surface: Advice to a couple to get engaged while sharing a holiday flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Gears mesh when their teeth interlock, so to mesh is to engage with one another.

clue.text: Turned over great book I have that's controversial

indicators.note: turned over means the book word is flipped and read backwards

parts.note: a tome is a large heavy book
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Someone flips through a big book that has caused a stir.
explanation.definitionFit: An emotive issue arouses strong feeling, which makes it contentious.

clue.text: Male announcing about one about to lose?

indicators.note: about here means surrounding the single letter

parts.note: stating means declaring or announcing

explanation.surface: A man announcing himself as a likely loser.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the proverb 'he who hesitates is lost', hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesitating, by the proverb, is the state that leads to being lost.

clue.text: Fruit drink that's pink I had knocked back inside

indicators.note: inside places the turned contraction within the colour word

parts.note: coral is a pinkish-orange colour

indicators.note: knocked back means turned round, so the contraction is read backwards

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone recalls downing a pink fruit drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' suggests drinking, fitting the surface, but here it reverses the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A cordial is a sweet concentrated fruit syrup diluted with water to make a soft drink.

clue.text: Police covering up evidence of debt that's abundant

indicators.note: the police word wraps around the debt note, covering it

parts.note: cops is informal for police
an IOU is a written acknowledgement of money owed

explanation.surface: Police hiding signs of debt that has piled up.
explanation.definitionFit: Copious means plentiful, a straightforward synonym for abundant.

clue.text: Subject to possible revision, feed friend

parts.note: to provision is to supply with food
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: Plans to feed a friend are not yet final.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done provisionally is tentative and may be changed later.

clue.text: Member of working group due to change in transition, possibly

indicators.note: to change the letters of these two words is to rearrange them
possibly says the letters may be put in another order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A worker in a labour movement facing upheaval during a period of change.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade unionist belongs to a union, an organised body of workers.

clue.text: Annoyed fishermen about a critical juncture

parts.note: cross means angry

indicators.note: about means the fishing word goes round the article

parts.note: rods are anglers, named for their fishing rods
taken as written

explanation.surface: Angry anglers gather around a decisive moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossroads is figuratively a point where a crucial decision must be made.

clue.text: Take off and wander around East with maiden

indicators.note: around means the wandering word surrounds the other two letters

parts.note: to rove is to roam or wander
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Someone sets off on a trip eastward, accompanied by a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove a garment is to take it off, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Explosive device in mint awfully close at hand

indicators.note: in places the explosive inside the scrambled letters
awfully suggests badly done, so the letters of mint are scrambled

parts.note: the word itself supplies the four letters to rearrange
a mine is a buried explosive

explanation.surface: A bomb hidden at the Royal Mint is about to go off.
explanation.definitionFit: Imminent describes something about to happen, near in time.

clue.text: Head off a lot of deaths? It's supposedly the best medicine

indicators.note: head off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: slaughter is killing on a large scale

explanation.surface: A grim question about mass death, then a cheery proverb.
explanation.walkthrough: SLAUGHTER without its first letter S leaves LAUGHTER; the grim surface hides the cheerful proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying 'laughter is the best medicine' claims that amusement heals.

clue.text: Person from North or South, and one from west of Europe

parts.note: an Iberian comes from Spain or Portugal, on the Iberian peninsula in western Europe

explanation.surface: A question of nationality: northerner, southerner or western European.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North or South' reads as a pair of choices; North belongs to the definition and South is just a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A Siberian lives in Siberia, the vast northern region of Russia.

clue.text: A line in heavy wind that stabilises ship

indicators.note: in puts the article and line inside the gust

parts.note: a blast is a strong gust
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rope that keeps a vessel steady in a gale.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballast is heavy material carried low in a vessel to keep it stable.

clue.text: Assassin decapitated American poet

indicators.note: decapitated means the head, or first letter, is cut off

parts.note: Walt Whitman was the poet of Leaves of Grass

explanation.surface: A killer beheads a famous American poet.
explanation.walkthrough: WHITMAN without its first letter W leaves HITMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A hit man is a hired killer, a slang synonym for assassin.

clue.text: Improperly deliver cards making married ladies perturbed

indicators.note: perturbed means agitated, so the letters of ladies are thrown about

parts.note: the word itself supplies the six letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A dealer upsets the wives at the bridge table by dealing badly.
explanation.definitionFit: To misdeal is to make an error in dealing cards to players.

clue.text: Flowery piece found in part of Bible

indicators.note: found in says the answer lies inside the Bible word

parts.note: the Old and New Testaments are the two parts of the Bible

explanation.surface: An ornate passage discovered in scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: The word to search is not printed: first find the Bible part, TESTAMENT, then the answer is the run of letters inside it once its outer letters are dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: The stamen is the pollen-bearing organ of a flower, so a floral part.

clue.text: Danger on rocky hillside for group still at the top?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: loose stones tumbling down a slope
second meaning: the veteran rock band still at the top of their profession

explanation.walkthrough: The 'rocky' hillside nods to rock music; the band has endured for decades.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rolling Stones are a long-lived British rock band, and rolling stones are also falling rocks.

clue.text: Food team-mate has demolished in first or second half

indicators.note: demolished means knocked down, so the half is rearranged
either half of the hyphenated word will do, since each holds the same four letters

parts.note: the hyphenated word is split into its two four-letter halves

explanation.surface: A footballer's teammate wolfed the food at half-time.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves, team and mate, are anagrams of each other and of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat is flesh eaten as food, and in older use food generally.

clue.text: Not for profit, in a way

indicators.note: in puts the profit word inside the other letters

parts.note: taken as written
ST is short for street, a way
gain is a synonym for profit

explanation.surface: An organisation that does not exist to make money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not for profit' reads as one familiar phrase, but the definition stops after 'for'.
explanation.definitionFit: Against is the opposite of for, as in votes for and against.

clue.text: French dramatist increasingly including fiction

indicators.note: including means the first word holds the second

parts.note: more and more means increasingly
a lie is an untrue story

explanation.surface: A playwright who puts ever more invention into his work.
explanation.definitionFit: Molière was the seventeenth-century French comic playwright of Tartuffe.

clue.text: Location or spot, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak signals a word spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: to spot something is to sight it

explanation.surface: A request for a place, or a particular point in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot' looks like a second definition meaning place, but it is the verb to see.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is the place where something is situated.

clue.text: In good US city, managed even accommodation for senior

parts.note: ran as in ran a business
NY is New York
even and flat both mean level

explanation.surface: A retiree who handled a New York move well finds somewhere to live.
explanation.walkthrough: A granny flat is a British term for a self-contained annexe attached to a family home for an elderly relative.
explanation.definitionFit: The annexe is built to house an older relative, so it is lodging for an elderly person.
